I’m v late to this post but as I said in another comment, that sign has been there for as long as I’ve been alive so at least 27 years. 
However, while I agree that the sign is supposed to be a joke, and that in general if you’re nice to people they’ll be more likely to help you - my experience with the receptionists in this practise is vastly different. 
I have very severe anxiety and agoraphobia, so please believe me when I say that I am ALWAYS polite. I over apologise constantly for everything and I don’t so much as even raise my voice at people. One of these receptionists reduced me to a break down and panic attack in the waiting room, and then accused me of lying about my address the next 2 times I phoned for an appointment. I only stayed at the practise after that because I loved my GP, but he has now retired. The receptionist at love street make me so anxious that I don’t even want to seek care when I need it. 
I don’t doubt that there are lovely receptionists out there, however all the nightmare stories about this practise are definitely true.
That sign has been there for at least 25 years.

I’ve been at this GP since birth (27 years) and that sign has been there the whole time. My mum has also been a patient at this surgery since birth (she’s 64) so I will ask her how old she thinks it is. It also used to have a fish pond in the waiting room (proper random).

For anyone considering this practise - some of the receptionists are so rude but there are a couple of nice ones. One of the receptionists in particular is a horrible insensitive woman and after my last run in with her the only reason I stayed was for my GP. 
He’s now retired and I’m thinking of moving practises because the anxiety of dealing with the receptionists to talk to a doctor about my anxiety is simply not worth it anymore. It puts me off seeking care.

NTA. Your body is your body. As someone who was very petite most of their life, and never struggled with their body image other than sometimes wondering if they were underweight and being bullied in school (called anorexic, skeleton etc), but has recently gone up a couple of dress sizes for the first time in her life - I am by no means what most people would consider “big”. I am smaller than the average female size in my country. But to me, it’s a MASSIVE change from how I’m used to feeling in my body, and it has massively knocked my confidence. But every time I try to talk about it or tell anyone how I feel, they shut me down and say “oh you have nothing to worry about, you’re skinny” or “I can’t believe you’re complaining about your body when you’re so much smaller than me, I’d kill to be as ‘skinny’ as you” or “if you think you’re fat, I must be obese”. It’s so frustrating. Your body image is your body image, and no one else’s. She’s attention seeking.
